SCRIPT_MUTATIONS: the queue tests up to six pull requests together; a batch size of five is not the size the queue rule states (SPEC-604 R1)
each member of a batch merges by a merge commit; a squash method rewrites the commits of every member (SPEC-604 R1, R3)
a pull request enters only with the queue label; a condition on another label name keeps every labelled pull request out (SPEC-604 R2)

queue_conditions:
      - base = dev
      - label = queue
      - draft
a draft never enters the queue; a condition that asks for a draft refuses every pull request ready for review (SPEC-604 R2)
a pull request with an unresolved review thread stays out; a bound every count meets admits it (SPEC-604 R2, R4)

merge_conditions:
      - base = dev
      - label = queue
      - -draft
      - "#review-threads-unresolved = 0"
      - check-success = ci

merge_conditions:
      - base = dev
      - label = queue
      - -draft
      - "#review-threads-unresolved = 0"
      - check-success = cj
a batch merges only after ci passes on it; a merge condition on a check no workflow produces never lets a green batch merge (SPEC-604 R3)
only the queue login takes the batch arm; a comparison every login meets lets a person on a queue branch skip the fragment (SPEC-604 R8)
only a head branch under the queue prefix takes the batch arm; a shorter prefix lets the queue login on another branch skip the fragment (SPEC-604 R8)
the head branch is compared over the whole queue prefix; a cut of another length never equals it, so a dependency-only batch is refused (SPEC-604 R8)
a queue batch is handed to the dependency-file rule; left with its own login it never reaches that rule, so a dependency-only batch is refused (SPEC-604 R8)
the queue checks one batch at a time; the default of five starts speculative batches side by side, each a full ci run (SPEC-604 R1)
the checks of a batch have a fixed timeout; auto applies none until the queue has a run history, then follows its usual run, which a long batch can outlast (SPEC-604 R1)
the merge conditions repeat the queue conditions; a merge list that differs makes the queue two-step, so a lone pull request that holds the tip of dev waits for a batch run (SPEC-604 R3)
